title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Tasting Basics
objectives: Taste a wine in a consistent order

steps.prompt: Put the tasting steps in order.
steps.explanation: Look, swirl to release aromas, smell, taste and only then conclude.

steps.prompt: A white wine is deep gold. What is the most likely explanation?
options: It has some age or oak
steps.explanation: Whites deepen in colour with age and time in oak. Very young, unoaked whites are pale lemon.

steps.prompt: Aromas that come from age, like honey, leather and nuts, are called ____ aromas.
steps.explanation: Primary aromas come from the grape, secondary from winemaking and tertiary from time.

steps.prompt: Which are part of a wine's structure?
steps.explanation: Structure is what you feel: sweetness, acidity, tannin, alcohol, body. Aromas and colour are separate parts of the note.

steps.prompt: Legs on a glass are a reliable sign of quality.
steps.explanation: Not true. They show alcohol and sugar, nothing about quality. Length of finish and balance tell you much more.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Look, smell, taste and conclude, every time
Colour tells age; aromas tell grape, winemaking and time
Structure is felt: acidity waters, tannin dries, alcohol warms
Balance and length are the clearest signs of quality
